A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DMesh++ and retain its central Minimum-Ball formulation. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the image-dominated final pages of v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original tessellation timings, 2D reconstruction and Reinforce-Ball ablations, and quantitative and qualitative 3D multi-view reconstruction results.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction results, including new 3D point-cloud comparisons, expanded multi-view benchmarks, memory measurements, a DTU failure example, and a physics simulation demonstration.

M1.justification: The reconstruction procedure changes substantively. v1 optimizes independent face probabilities, regularizes their mean, and derives point real values; v2 directly optimizes and regularizes point real values (Appendix 8). The revised pipeline also omits v1's explicit non-manifold-removal operation. Minimum-Ball, nearest-neighbor caching, subdivision, anti-aliasing, and Reinforce-Ball remain; Reinforce-Ball's relocation is not a method removal.

E1.justification: v2 adds dedicated 3D reconstruction from oriented and unoriented point clouds, real-image reconstruction on DTU, and a downstream bouncing-ball simulation. These extend task and input-domain coverage beyond v1's 2D point-cloud and synthetic multi-view reconstruction studies. Thingi10K, Objaverse, fonts, and complex drawings were already represented in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated point-cloud comparators PSR, VoroMesh, and PoNQ alongside DMesh. All appear in Table 2; the larger Table 3 includes PSR, PoNQ, and DMesh. The multi-view comparator set remains Remeshing, DMTet, FlexiCubes, GShell, and DMesh.

E3.justification: The 20-model hand-selected multi-view evaluation becomes evaluations on 50 selected models and 500 randomly selected models, the latter split equally between closed and open surfaces. New point-cloud protocols use 200K Poisson-disk samples and distinguish oriented from unoriented inputs. GPU memory is added to scaling evaluation. Font downsampling is now stated as 0.005 cells, whereas v1 describes approximately half the initial 0.005 grid spacing; this documentation change does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a controlled renderer translation experiment testing visibility gradients (Figure 14), a topology-evolution visualization (Figure 3), memory-scaling analysis, and a DTU failure case (Figure 21). The Reinforce-Ball ablations are retained as Table 6 and Figure 24, rather than newly introduced. v1's separate self-occluded-vase failure illustration is omitted.

E5.justification: Both versions report five trials and averaged measurements for tessellation scaling. Neither introduces reported seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for reconstruction results. Expanded result tables retain aggregate point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds point-cloud results, 500-model reconstruction results, and memory savings reaching 96% in 2D and 75% in 3D. Its 50-model multi-view table replaces v1's 20-model aggregate: DMesh++ CD changes from 0.127 to 0.342, both scaled by 10^-3, under different evaluation conditions. These are not same-setting performance changes. Font and Reinforce-Ball numbers remain unchanged; several colored-example counts and timings disappear.

T1.justification: v2 Equation (3) reverses the signed-distance definition from radius minus nearest-point distance to nearest-point distance minus radius, correcting its sign relative to the positive empty-ball test. However, Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the old sign. The real-loss definition also changes from averaging face probabilities to averaging point real values. Lemma 3.2, its proof, and the Reinforce-Ball gradient derivation remain.

C1.justification: v1 presents Minimum-Ball and adaptive-resolution Reinforce-Ball as paired central contributions. v2 centers its abstract and contribution list on efficient reconstruction, explicitly adds memory reduction and 3D point-cloud reconstruction claims, and relegates Reinforce-Ball to an experimental appendix component. Its conclusion acknowledges residual non-manifold errors instead of presenting their elimination as an available capability.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits real-image applicability because of its simple rendering model and assumed lighting knowledge, supported by the DTU failure case. It adds sparse-point-cloud and computational-cost limitations and conjectures an expressiveness/non-manifoldness trade-off. It also attributes GShell's high average error to outlier failures. v1's detailed explanation of Reinforce-Ball's difficulty in 3D is shortened to a limitation statement.

D1.justification: v2 adds density-based point-cloud initialization instructions, dedicated 3D point-cloud hyperparameters and baseline settings, an explicit triangle-quality loss formula, and Phong/directional-light rendering details. It removes v1's detailed 2D DMesh setup, four-epoch colored-reconstruction schedule, and DNA source/10K-point initialization disclosure. Hardware and the stated project access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting point-cloud reconstruction, DTU, 2D Gaussian Splatting, and t-SNE, while removing works including Meshtron and NeRF. It refines the description of earlier mesh methods to acknowledge local connectivity changes. The three-part related-work organization and central positioning as an efficient successor to DMesh remain.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: Section 4 becomes a short reconstruction overview, detailed operations and losses move into Appendix 8, and Reinforce-Ball moves into Appendix 10. Experiments are regrouped by reconstruction task, the introduction is rewritten, and the discussion becomes a conclusion with revised limitations and future directions.

P2.justification: v2 adds conceptual, topology-evolution, point-cloud, simulation, renderer-test, and DTU figures, expands the timing plot with memory panels, and redraws the pipeline. It adds and reorganizes comparison tables, relocates Reinforce-Ball displays, combines earlier full-page drawings into Figure 18, and removes much of the colored reconstruction gallery.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence beyond v1's small, selectively chosen multi-view benchmark through broader random-model evaluation, dedicated point-cloud comparisons, memory measurements, and a controlled renderer test. The DTU failure example and clearer applicability limits also improve claim calibration. These gains outweigh lost implementation details and remaining inconsistencies: the corrected signed-distance sign is not propagated to appendix pseudocode, and the claim of outperforming DMesh on every point-cloud metric conflicts with Table 2's non-manifold-vertex values.
